A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MDCure and MDCureRM. Their complete text, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated between versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations, data-scaling experiments, prompt and scoring ablations, and human evaluation of MDCureRM.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds generator comparisons, PPO experiments, general-capability evaluations, and instruction-diversity analysis.

M1.justification: V1 proposes training a custom instruction generator as future work. V3 implements this extension using MDCureRM rewards and PPO to train LLAMA3.1-8B-Instruct, producing instructions without subsequent filtering (Section 5.5). The original prompt-generation pipeline, six-criterion reward model, and filtering procedure remain.

E1.justification: V3 adds mathematics, coding, and general-knowledge evaluation through GSM8K, MBPP, and MMLU (Section 5.6), plus Tulu V2 instruction data for diversity analysis. NewSHead training coverage and the original multi-document, long-context, and few-shot scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The main downstream comparator roster remains. V3 adds explicit generator comparisons involving LLAMA3.1-70B and the PPO-trained generator, and diversity comparisons against HotpotQA, WikiHop, and Tulu V2. V1's preliminary negative LLAMA2-13B generator comparison disappears. PRIMERA/QAMDEN data comparisons are relocated rather than removed.

E3.justification: V3 introduces 12K-sample generator comparisons, PPO training over 72K samples for one epoch, OLMES general-capability evaluation, and matched 12K-sample diversity analysis. It also normalizes summarization evaluation scores to 0–100, affecting aggregate scores. The established supervised fine-tuning and zero-shot evaluation settings remain unchanged; these additions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds investigations of open-source generator substitution, PPO-based generation, preservation of general capabilities, and instruction diversity and complexity, together with illustrative instruction examples. The original prompt-template and scoring-criterion ablations remain in Appendix A; their relocation is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: For summarization-judge validation, v3 newly reports human agreement using Krippendorff's alpha and explicitly identifies Pearson correlations with human scores (Tables 15–16). V1 already described two annotators and 500 samples per dataset, so additional annotation is not established. Neither version reports new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V3 adds generator, PPO, general-capability, diversity, and evaluator-validation results. Retained ZeroScrolls results also change: Jamba's score moves from 35.1 to 34.1 and unfiltered LLAMA3.1-70B from 37.2 to 34.9. Summarization-score normalization changes averages and the headline improvement from 75.5% to 75.1%, without establishing performance gains. Detailed subtask results for Qwen2+PRIMERA/QAMDEN and ProLong+MDCure disappear, while their aggregate comparisons remain.

T1.justification: The reward regression, score transformation, and weighted aggregation retain their mathematical substance. V3 supplies no new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation; PPO is introduced as an applied training procedure.

C1.justification: V3 expands the abstract, introduction, and conclusion to claim effective open-source generation and PPO integration, including small generators surpassing proprietary models without further filtering. It also explicitly positions MDCure as the first framework for high-quality MD-focused post-training datasets. These extend v1's central generation-and-filtering contribution.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations concerning preserved general capabilities, instruction diversity, and open-source generation's cost advantages. Its limitations newly emphasize abstractive rather than extractive instruction coverage, while removing substantive discussions of costly scaling beyond small document clusters, prompt sensitivity, and amplification of source biases. These changes alter the stated applicability boundaries and qualifications.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds PPO hardware, epoch count, batch size, learning rates, and LoRA information; the diversity analysis identifies its parser and complexity scorer. Existing supervised-training and reward-model details remain. The code link is retained, but v3 drops v1's explicit statement that models are available; actual resource withdrawal cannot be inferred.

R1.justification: V3 substantially strengthens positioning around open-model post-training and reinforcement learning from AI feedback, adding discussion and citations such as Phi-4, Tulu 3, Constitutional AI, and RLAIF. It trims older multi-document and instruction-tuning background and adds literature supporting the new evaluation and diversity analyses.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, conclusions, and limitations undergo substantial rewriting. Original Sections 5.4–5.5 move to Appendix A, while generator and general-capability experiments occupy the main results narrative. Instruction-format and extended-context construction explanations also move into reorganized appendices.

P2.justification: V3 reorganizes the main and full-results tables around model-size comparisons and adds blue/yellow highlighting. It separates retained pre-training-data comparisons into Table 3 and adds tables for generators, general capabilities, examples, diversity, and evaluator agreement. Ablation tables relocate to the appendix; prompt Figures 4–18 remain visually unchanged despite relocation.

improvement.justification: V3 provides useful new evidence about generator flexibility and general-capability retention, and makes the existing summarization-judge validation assessable through numerical agreement statistics. These gains are tempered by claims about SOTA proprietary generators supported only against GPT-3.5-Turbo, removal of concrete limitations, and a newly inconsistent ProLong ZeroScrolls score: 32.2 in Table 1 versus 33.6 in Tables 2 and 18. The evidence improves overall, but the reporting and qualification problems limit the net gain.
